target_customer: Construction project managers and general contractors who build and update project schedules
problem: Baseline schedules are built by hand from project documents and updated slowly as projects change. Karmen builds and updates them with AI.

founders.name: Jonas Ebrahimi
founders.background_notes: Education not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Naman Wahi
education: Master's in AI and Machine Learning, Imperial College London

technical_complexity.rationale: Extracting schedule logic from construction documents and keeping it consistent is hard applied AI, but doable for two engineers with an nPlan background.

defensibility.rationale: Scheduling workflows can be copied by incumbents with existing data; no moat sourced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Procore announced AI scheduling agents at Groundbreak 2024 per a vendor blog, which is a competitor source; no acquisition of Karmen found.

market_need_then: Construction schedules are manual and delays are costly per the company pitch. No quantified demand evidence was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses karmenai.com; the exact karmen domain is used by an unrelated French fintech.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand coverage; shares its name with a French fintech and others.

pivots.from: AI assistant for project managers handling invoices, RFIs and change orders
pivots.why: Not stated; the YC launch post describes the earlier admin focus and the YC page describes scheduling

outcome_analysis: Karmen is a two-person Fall 2024 company that moved from construction admin automation toward scheduling. No funding confirmation, customer or exit was found beyond a 2026 conference appearance, so the outcome is unknown with a thin evidence base.
notes: One directory lists 500K seed for an AI construction scheduling company without investors; unverified, no round recorded. The Karmen funding search mostly returned a French fintech and others. Founding date inferred only from YC batch. Competitor search found no sources dated near the batch; competitor names in takeover risk come from 2026 vendor blogs.
